selectedAlternative.implementation: Bounded original Tj/TJ replacement and uniform-paragraph typesetting using the existing encoding and natural glyph metrics. Editor defaults to paragraph reflow without changing font size, spacing or scale. Original line/text state is restored; neighboring blocks stay fixed. The legacy fitToSpace engine option remains tested but is not exposed or invoked by the editor.
selectedAlternative.scope: Printable ASCII runs in non-symbolic Base-14 Type1 fonts or Identity-H CID fonts with one-to-one ToUnicode maps; unknown simple embedded fonts remain read-only. Same-page, left-aligned uniform paragraphs support longer replacements, cross-line selections and explicit line breaks within bounded width/height. Overflow refuses instead of shrinking, squeezing, overlapping neighbors or paginating. Graphics/annotations prevent growth outside the original area; intersecting links and unindexed text prevent reflow. No mixed-style paragraph reflow, font substitution, XObject editing or visible scan reconstruction.
selectedAlternative.accessibility: Unique page MCID ownership and exact ActualText are verified and repaired; the reopened expected tag graph and outlines are checked. Ambiguous/shared semantics refuse editing.
verification: paragraph-layout.test.ts and source-paragraph.test.ts: natural wrapping, cross-line selection, overflow, linked/shared/hidden text refusal, original text state and ActualText/outline preservation

tests/browser/paragraph-reflow.spec.ts: preview/review/apply/undo, normal and cropped/rotated exports with independent qpdf/Poppler/Python font, footer geometry and outside-paragraph pixel checks; reopened export canvas equals applied preview canvas
tests/browser/selected-text.spec.ts with independent qpdf/Poppler/Python font, baseline, bounds and outside-pixel checks
selectedAlternative.integration: Current-page editor dialog with actual exported-PDF preview, explicit review, immutable source revisions and undo/redo
selectedAlternative.remaining: Broader Unicode/font/layout corpus and manual accessibility/Windows platform checks; no universal PDF editing claim
